key_insight: FETI-SAW combines domain decomposition with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space to stabilize iteration counts across subdomain counts, frequencies, and mesh sizes.
engineering_relevance: The method targets large, ill-conditioned finite element systems arising in high-frequency, multiphysics surface acoustic wave device simulations.
method: Partition the finite element problem using finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI).
Construct a physically motivated coarse space based on Rayleigh waves.
Apply a Dirichlet preconditioner with coarse-space correction to the Lagrange multiplier system.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on interdigital transducers and SAW resonators demonstrate efficiency; accompanying MATLAB and C++ source codes are provided.
watch_item: The abstract gives no quantitative speedups or setup costs, so practical gains require checking coarse-space construction and solver performance on the target device.
paper_title: A Novel Two-Level Domain Decomposition Method with Physically Motivated Coarse Space for Surface Acoustic Wave Device Simulations
